text:
marta: quick postmortem from the deploy this morning — saw a 35% drop in prefix hit-rate after the autoscale event, followed by sustained higher tail latency. tagging you all because it touches kernel fallback and kv-keying.
kai: saw it too, timeline looks like: scale-up -> priming job starts -> hit-rate spikes briefly -> ~90s later hit-rate collapses and stays low. :thinking_face:
allen: logs show a flurry of evictions right around the collapse. possible key namespace mismatch? some keys were 32-byte hex, others had a redis-escaped prefix.
sasha: hmm can you paste the seeder job command and the deploy config? wondering if we accidentally switched seeder from guided-mode to headless-generator.
marta: here are the two commands we ran (from ops runbook):

```
# guided prefill
infractl seeder run --mode guided --cardinality 1000 --prefix-policy route-aware

# headless seed (fallback)
infractl seeder run --mode headless --rps 50 --templates default
```

marta: the deploy trigger picked headless due to a bad guard in the rollout script (falsey env var). so we basically started an unkeyed synthetic flood that didn't align with real prefix distribution.
kai: that explains the fragmentation. headless created lots of low-cardinality keys that pushed eviction pressure on hot shards.
allen: additionally profiling the runtime around the collapse shows we hit the kernel fallback path for attention matmul on the new quantized build. fallback increased per-token CPU which delayed KV writes, compounding eviction timing.
sasha: is the kernel fallback deterministic for those sequences? could be sequence-length dependent.
kai: yes, fallback triggers when sequence%16 != 0 for our fused kernel. most seeded sequences were odd-length because of template tokenization differences.
marta: immediate mitigation: rollback to previous seeder config and re-run guided prefill. also pin the kernel selectors to the old heuristic until we fix the odd-length case.
allen: put a temporary rate-cap on synthetic seeding during autoscale windows? e.g., cap to 10% of node capacity from the rollout script.
sasha: i'll open a small PR to make the seeder mode explicit (fail deploy if unset) and add a canary gate for the new kernel selector.
marta: can someone capture the KV key histogram and eviction traces from the nodes that hit the collapse? need to attach to the ticket.
allen: grabbing histograms now — will paste to the incident ticket in a minute.
deploy-bot: deploy/1774 succeeded by marta — note: rollback issued to seeder config  (manual) :white_check_mark:
kai: follow-ups: (1) fix seeder-mode guard, (2) add seeding rate-limiter in rollout script, (3) patch kernel selector to prefer fused kernel for odd lengths or normalize sequences, (4) add eviction alarms that trigger a prewarm rollback.
marta: agree. i'll create the RFC for normalized seeding + new kernel guard. thanks everyone, learned a lot about how keyboard-level seeding interacts with runtime kernels. :thumbsup:
